guide.title: Moving from Google Authenticator?
guide.step1: Open Google Authenticator on your phone.
guide.step2: Tap the menu (⋮ or ☰) → Transfer accounts → Export accounts.
guide.step3: Select the accounts and tap Next — one or more QR codes appear.
guide.step4: Screenshot every QR code (swipe to the next one) and drop the screenshots here — or point the Camera tab at them.
guide.otherApps: Other apps (Authy, 1Password, Microsoft Authenticator…) and most websites also show a QR code when you set up 2FA — screenshots of those work too.

guide.chromeCopied: Address copied — paste it into Chrome
guide.chrome2: Next to Export passwords, click Download file and confirm with your computer password.
guide.chromeNote: Edge, Brave, Arc, Opera and Vivaldi export the same file from their password settings.
guide.onePassword1: In the 1Password desktop app, choose File → Export and pick your account.
guide.onePassword2: Enter your account password and choose 1PUX — it keeps 2FA codes and tags. CSV works too.
guide.onePasswordNote: Archived items, credit cards and notes are left out. 2FA codes are saved and linked to their login.
guide.browserCopied: Address copied — paste it into your browser
guide.dashlane2: Open the Vault menu at the top left, choose Settings → Export data and click Export to CSV.
guide.dashlane3: Drop the downloaded .zip below as it is — no need to unpack it.
guide.dashlaneNote: 2FA codes come along and are linked to their login. Notes, IDs and payment cards in the export are left out; Dashlane can't export passkeys.
guide.otherNote: Any CSV with a url and a password column works — the columns are detected automatically.
